questions.prompt: Your company has zero data retention (ZDR) with Anthropic for its main organization. A team opens a second organization. What do Anthropic's docs say?

options.text: ZDR copies over to every organization under the same account automatically.
options.explanation: The docs say the opposite: enablement does not automatically extend to other organizations.

options.text: Each new organization needs ZDR enabled separately by the account team.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic enables ZDR per organization.

options.text: A second organization can't be created while ZDR is active.
options.explanation: The docs don't say that. They say each organization needs its own enablement.

questions.prompt: According to OpenAI's safety guide, when is human review of outputs especially critical?

options.text: Only when the output is longer than one page.
options.explanation: The guide doesn't use length. It points to high-stakes domains and code generation.

options.text: Only during the first week after launch, while staff learn the tool.
options.explanation: The guide recommends review wherever possible, not for a fixed period.

options.text: In high-stakes domains, and for code generation.
options.explanation: Right. It also says reviewers need access to the information to check the output.

questions.prompt: Which policy rule is the easiest to check?

options.text: "IT checks each new project's retention setting before go-live."
options.explanation: Right. Someone can see whether the check happened, and OpenAI's data controls show the setting per project.

options.text: "Everyone uses AI responsibly and with good judgement at work."
options.explanation: Nobody can test this. It doesn't say who does what.

options.text: "Teams should think about privacy when they use AI tools."
options.explanation: This names a topic, not an action that someone can check.
